chunks: Indeed, for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, there are two knowledges: a knowledge which He made manifest to His angels, His Prophets, and His Messengers. So whatever He made manifest to His angels, His Messengers, and His Prophets, we have known it. And there is a knowledge which He kept exclusively to Himself; then when something from it becomes manifest by Allah's will, He informs us of that, and it was presented to the Imams who were before us.

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim; and Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-'Amraki ibn Ali—altogether—from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام, similarly to it.

key_terms.أَنْبِيَاءَهُ: His Prophets, to whom Allah reveals knowledge.
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: The Imams, who receive divinely taught knowledge.
key_terms.رُسُلَهُ: His Messengers, entrusted with divine communication.
key_terms.عِلْمَيْنِ: Two categories or kinds of knowledge.
key_terms.مَلَائِكَتَهُ: His angels, recipients of divinely disclosed knowledge.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about Allah’s exclusive knowledge and the knowledge of the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith describes two categories of divine knowledge: one that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, discloses to the angels, Prophets, and Messengers, and which the Imams also know; and another that Allah keeps exclusively with Himself until He wills to disclose something from it. It highlights the special divinely granted knowledge of the Imams while affirming that ultimate, unrestricted knowledge remains with Allah alone.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad and Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Sama’at, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said: ‘For Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Blessed and High there are two (types of) Knowledges – a Knowledge He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Manifested upon the Angels and His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Prophets<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> and His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Rasools<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>. So whatever was Manifested upon His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Angels, and His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Rasools<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, and His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Prophets<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, we<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> know it; and a Knowledge He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is exclusive with it. So whenever Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> begins regarding something from it, He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Teaches us<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> that and it is displayed upon the Imams<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> who were before us<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>’.

Ali Bin Muhammad and Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Musa Bin Al Qasim and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, altogether, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> – similar to it.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hassan from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Shammun from ‘Abdallah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from ‘Abdallah ibn al-Qasim from Sama‘a from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, has two kinds of knowledge. One kind is that which is revealed to the angels, the prophets the Messenger of Allah. Whatever is revealed to the angels, the Messenger of Allah and the prophets, is known to us also. The other is the kind which is exclusively for Allah. When Allah wants to make public anything from it is taught to us first and it is presented to the Imams before us also.”

Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hassan have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Musa ibn al-Qasim and Muhammad ibn Yahya from al-‘Amrakiy ibn Ali all of them from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s.) a similar Hadith.
